clue.text: Registers arrival of European at hotel, say

indicators.note: 'say' tells the solver that the phrase is spoken and the spelling is taken from how it sounds

parts.note: a European is a Czech, and a hotel is an inn, so this is a Czech's inn

explanation.surface: A hotel clerk notes that a European guest has turned up and signed in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Say' signals a homophone: a Czech's inn, a European's hotel, spoken aloud gives the phrase meaning registers at a hotel. 'of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Signing the register at a hotel reception on arrival is the phrasal verb used for guests.

clue.text: Down Transfer worker to position of supervisor?

parts.note: a hand is a manual worker, as in farmhand
a supervisor stands over the workers, so the position is over

explanation.surface: A manager wonders about promoting a labourer to oversee the others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Down' at the start is the column heading printed beside the clue, not part of the clue itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A handover is the passing of responsibility or control from one party to another, so a transfer.

clue.text: Chapter on poet is easy to understand

indicators.note: in a down clue 'on' means placed after, so the chapter letter comes first

parts.note: Edward Lear was the English poet of nonsense verse such as The Owl and the Pussycat

explanation.surface: A reader finds a chapter about a poet straightforward.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain or lucid writing is described as easy to follow.

clue.text: Mostly quiet types?

parts.note: read literally, the greater part of people who say nothing: the political phrase for ordinary voters who do not speak out

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names the large mass of citizens who hold views but do not voice them publicly.

clue.text: Showing signs of potential growth, hospital raised a bit of money

indicators.note: in a down clue 'raised' means the word is turned upwards, read from bottom to top

parts.note: san is short for sanatorium, a kind of hospital
a cent is a small coin, a bit of money

explanation.surface: A hospital, showing early promise, collected a little cash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' works because this is a down clue, so the hospital word reads upwards; 'hospital' looks like part of the growth picture but only supplies letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Something emerging and just beginning to develop is at an early budding stage.

clue.text: Travel document is needed to enter American state

indicators.note: 'needed to enter' says the word is goes inside the state abbreviation

parts.note: VA is the postal abbreviation for Virginia

explanation.surface: A traveller needs the right paperwork to get into a US state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needed' is a link; 'American state' points to the two-letter postal code, not a full state name.
explanation.definitionFit: A passport endorsement permitting entry to a country is a document for travelling.

clue.text: Wicked! Endless drinks for members of the community

indicators.note: 'Endless' means the last letter of the word before is cut off

parts.note: vile means wicked or evil
lagers are beers, drinks

explanation.surface: An exclamation of delight at a never-ending round at the pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wicked!' looks like slang praise but is the plain sense evil, and 'Endless' applies to it, not to the drinks.
explanation.definitionFit: Residents of a small rural settlement make up its local population.

clue.text: Piercing cry, one stifled during film

indicators.note: 'stifled during' says the letter for one is smothered inside the film title

parts.note: Shrek is the animated film about an ogre
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone tries to stop themselves screaming in the cinema.
explanation.definitionFit: A shrill high-pitched scream is a sharp sound of fear or delight.

clue.text: Make light of this plant?

parts.note: a paper lamp from the Far East gives light, and a plant with papery orange seed cases shares its name

explanation.definitionFit: Physalis alkekengi has inflated orange husks resembling paper lamps from Asia, hence its common name.

clue.text: A foreign source of water that's off

parts.note: un is the French for a, a foreign word
a well is a source of water

explanation.surface: Someone abroad drinks from a water source that has gone bad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's' is a link before the definition 'off', meaning ill.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling off means feeling poorly or sick.

clue.text: Accordingly companion is taken in by short, fat student

indicators.note: the companion's letters are absorbed inside the word for accordingly

parts.note: so means therefore, accordingly
CH stands for Companion of Honour, a British order

indicators.note: 'short' means the word for fat loses its last letter

parts.note: lard is pig fat

explanation.surface: A friend is drawn in by a plump young learner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Accordingly' is a crossword staple for so; 'short' applies only to 'fat', which is a noun here, not an adjective describing the student.
explanation.definitionFit: A learned person or one holding a study award at a university is a pupil of learning.

clue.text: Ran out, getting flustered

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held 'Ran out, getting flustered (8)' has no definition and an anagram of RAN OUT gives only six of the eight letters; the clue appears cut short and no source gives the full text.

clue.text: Tidy kitchen at last, having had meal

indicators.note: 'at last' picks the final letter of the word kitchen

parts.note: having eaten, so eaten

explanation.surface: Someone finally clears up the kitchen after dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: To smarten or put in order is to make neat.

clue.text: Foreign painter working in timeshares

indicators.note: 'working' suggests the letters are operated on and rearranged

explanation.surface: An overseas artist is busy at holiday flats he shares.
explanation.walkthrough: 'working' rearranges the twelve letters of IN TIMESHARES.
explanation.definitionFit: The French artist was a leading Fauvist, so a painter from abroad.

clue.text: Old family member taking journey round river

indicators.note: 'round' says the journey word wraps around the other letters

parts.note: a ride is a journey
a gran is a grandmother, a family member

explanation.surface: An elderly relative goes on a trip around a waterway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking' is a link; the river forms part of the border between the USA and Mexico.
explanation.definitionFit: The great watercourse forms part of the US-Mexico border.

clue.text: Old giant's obscure language

indicators.note: 'obscure' means the letters are muddled and made unclear

parts.note: the possessive adds no letter

explanation.surface: An ancient giant speaks an unclear tongue.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means a mock or debased form of Latin, a made-up tongue.

clue.text: Don't mind so much about such an ideal example?

parts.note: to mind is to object, so minding less is objecting less
on means about, concerning

explanation.surface: Someone is urged to be less fussed by a model of good behaviour.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as OBJECT LESS ON: 'Don't mind so much about' gives the whole run.
explanation.definitionFit: A practical illustration of a principle, used as a model to teach from.

clue.text: Looking embarrassed after fish is burnt

indicators.note: 'after' means the colour word comes after the fish in a down entry

parts.note: char is a fish of the trout family
red, as in red in the face

explanation.surface: A cook blushes after burning the fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Scorched black by fire describes food overcooked.

clue.text: Love tucking into flavoursome snack

indicators.note: 'tucking into' means placing one letter inside the word for flavoursome

parts.note: tasty means full of flavour
love is nil, zero in tennis scoring, written O

explanation.surface: Someone eats a delicious snack with affection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tucking into' looks like eating but puts O inside TASTY.
explanation.definitionFit: A toasted sandwich is a light bite sold in cafes.

clue.text: Car sped round bend, right?

indicators.note: 'round' says sped wraps around the letter for bend

parts.note: tore means rushed or sped
a U-bend is a curve shaped like the letter U

explanation.surface: A driver raced round a corner and kept right.
explanation.definitionFit: An open car built for long-distance driving is a type of vehicle.

clue.text: Every so often, woman meets with university friend

indicators.note: 'meets with' joins the woman's name to the rest side by side

parts.note: Ann is a woman's name
an ally is a friend

explanation.surface: A woman sees a college friend now and again.
explanation.definitionFit: Once a year is a regular interval, occasionally.

clue.text: Suffered, having done badly in exams, not getting a first

indicators.note: 'not getting a first' means the first letter is removed, with a pun on first-class degrees

parts.note: having failed

explanation.surface: A student did poorly in exams and missed a first-class degree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a first' sounds like a top degree but removes the first letter F.
explanation.definitionFit: To have been ill or troubled is to have suffered.

clue.text: Dispatched soldiers to protect a politician

indicators.note: 'to protect' means sent surrounds the letter a to guard it

parts.note: sent means dispatched
OR stands for other ranks, ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: Troops were sent to guard a politician.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of an upper legislative house is an elected lawmaker.

clue.text: Flashy displays organised in castle

indicators.note: 'organised' means the letters of castle are arranged into a new order

explanation.surface: Showy spectacles staged at a castle.
explanation.definitionFit: The French loanword means brilliant show or striking success.

clue.text: River going through pretty neighbourhood

indicators.note: 'going through' says the answer runs across the two words that follow

explanation.surface: A waterway flows through a lovely area.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits across preTTY NEighbourhood; the Tyne flows through Newcastle in north-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: The English waterway reaches the sea at Tynemouth.

clue.text: Campanologists' violent exchange?

parts.note: bell-ringers' sound echoes the term for a heated fight or quarrel

explanation.definitionFit: A noisy fierce argument is named after the sound of bells.
